chunks: For the mu'adhdhin, Allah forgives him as far as his sight reaches and as far as his voice reaches in the sky. Every moist and dry thing that hears him affirms him as truthful. He has a share from every one who prays with him in his mosque, and he has a good deed from every one who prays by his voice.

key_terms.الْمُؤَذِّنُ: the one who gives the call to prayer
key_terms.بَصَرِهِ: his sight; indicating the extent of reward
key_terms.حَسَنَةٌ: a good deed recorded for him
key_terms.رَطْبٍ: every moist thing that hears the call
key_terms.صَوْتِهِ: his voice; the reach of his call
key_terms.مَسْجِدِهِ: his mosque; the place where people join the prayer
key_terms.يَابِسٍ: every dry thing that hears the call

ai.seo_question: What reward does the mu'adhdhin receive in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the immense reward and forgiveness granted to the mu'adhdhin who calls people to salat. It highlights both the cosmic witness to the adhan and the continuing reward the mu'adhdhin receives through the worship of those who respond to his call.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.882 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:

"For the mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer), Allah (swt) forgives him as far as his sight and voice reach into the sky. Every moist and dry thing that hears him bears witness to his truth. For every person who prays with him in his mosque, he receives a share, and for every person who prays due to hearing his call, he earns a good deed."
